summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with pleuritic chest pain, fever, cough, and hypotension following a clinic visit. Evaluation ruled out acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, and pneumonia. Cardiac enzymes were stable, EKG unchanged, and CT angiography showed no PE but revealed bibasilar atelectasis and peribronchial thickening consistent with acute bronchitis. Orthostatic hypotension and elevated creatinine suggested volume depletion, which improved with IV fluids. Hypoglycemia occurred due to a higher-than-usual insulin dose and reduced oral intake, resolving with dietary correction. The patient improved with antibiotics, cough suppression, and fluid resuscitation, and was discharged home in fair condition with stable vital signs and improved symptoms.
